newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DSM Q3 results hit by margin squeeze.
newsitem.headline: DSM Q3 results hit by margin squeeze.

text.p: Dutch petrochemicals group DSM NV reported lower than expected third quarter earnings on Tuesday, saying its results were hit by a margin squeeze.
Net profit fell to 178 million guilders ($104 million) from 234 million in the third quarter of 1995. Analysts had forecast a net profit of 181 to 212 million guilders.
DSM NV said earnings were squeezed at both ends by lower prices and higher feedstock costs which led to narrower margins.
"This (lower profit) was mainly due to lower margins caused on the one hand by lower prices and on the other by higher feedstock costs, especially for naphtha," it said.
Sales volumes had risen for almost all of its main products, it added.
DSM said it expected the supply and demand situation for its main products to remain good during the coming months.
However, fourth quarter results would be affected by higher feedstock costs and by several planned maintenance shutdowns.
"We expect that it will only be possible to pass on a part of the increase in feedstock costs via the prices of our products," DSM said.
"All things considered, we maintain our previous forecast that 1996 will be a good year," it added. ($1=1.710 Guilder)
